xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3286: Workspace parity with Subspace: first-class shared workspaces, target-scoped recall, status history, session briefing

plan.title: Workspace parity with Subspace: first-class shared workspaces, target-scoped recall, status history, session briefing
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The canonical PRD (drafts/pan-3286.md on overdeck-state) deliberately structures this as one issue: items are coupled through shared files (searchMemory in src/lib/memory/cli.ts feeds both target-scoped search and cross-workspace injection; Sidebar.tsx carries both the rail filter and the phase badge) and an explicit ordering constraint (rail filter lands before phase UI). blocks edges inside one plan model these dependencies; sibling issues would race on the same files.

narratives.Problem: PAN-1990 ported Subspace's workspace storage model (UUID-keyed registry, per-workspace memory homes, two doors) but not its premise: a workspace as a long-lived user-owned lens targeting any repo directory. Scratch workspaces can only target the project primary path, there is no relocate/dry-run, no target-scoped or history recall, no timeline/read CLI, SessionStart injects nothing, non-issue turns get no cross-workspace context, memory-synthesized phase is invisible for main/scratch rows, and boot seeding floods the sidebar with dozens of pipeline feature-* worktrees presented as user workspaces.
narratives.Proposal: Close the gaps additively per the canonical PRD: --target-path and --dry-run on pan workspace new; relocateWorkspace writer + pan workspace relocate; pan memory search --target; workspace-addressable status/summary with --history; pan memory timeline and containment-checked pan memory read; a SessionStart briefing composed from local artifacts with per-session dedup; same-project cross-workspace injection for null-issue turns; memoryPhase in the registry list DTO with badges for non-issue rows; sidebar/Cmd-K default filter to main/scratch/favorited with a collapsed pipeline-worktrees count row; rebuild-workspaces archives terminal-issue rows. All registry access stays behind the two doors.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Per-workspace boards, threads, notes, tasks, transcripts, or diffs storage (PRD D-10)
- Renaming or restructuring memory homes on disk (PRD D-2)
- Any change to issue-workspace creation/teardown or pipeline-phase derivation for issue rows (PRD D-1)
- A standalone `pan workspace plan` verb (PRD D-4 folds it into --dry-run)
- New LLM calls at SessionStart (PRD D-7/NFR-6)
- Removing or deleting issue-kind registry rows (presentation filter + archive only, PRD D-13)
- Making `pan memory read` reach anything outside the resolved memory home, including ~/.claude JSONL session files (PRD D-9/NFR-4)

autoDecisions.summary: Lower the xBRIEF from the existing canonical PRD on overdeck-state instead of authoring a new PRD.
autoDecisions.rationale: drafts/pan-3286.md (259 lines, verified 2026-07-29 against main) already meets the prd-authoring standard; re-verification against feature/pan-3286 @ 5c2886b195 confirmed every code anchor. The workspace copy adds an addendum correcting only stale paths (sync-sources/skills/, db.ts wiring, injection test path, configuration/workspaces.mdx).

autoDecisions.summary: Keep one plan with sizeJustification instead of splitting into sibling issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: Items are coupled by shared files and an explicit PRD ordering constraint; blocks edges serialize them correctly, while sibling issues would race on src/lib/memory/cli.ts, src/cli/commands/memory.ts, and Sidebar.tsx.

Every item is an additive leaf surface (new flag, new subcommand, presentation filter) whose defects surface immediately at its own named tests or typecheck; no downstream item encodes assumptions about another item's internal structure, so an inspection gate would rubber-stamp mechanical diffs. Shared-file collisions are handled with blocks edges.

items.title: Add --target-path to pan workspace new

narrative.Action: Per PRD WI-1 (FR-1, D-3): add a --target-path <dir> option to WorkspaceNewOptions and workspaceNewCommand in src/cli/commands/workspace-scratch.ts (option wiring in workspace.ts). When given, the resolved absolute path replaces project.config.path as the scratch workspace path; validate it is an existing directory, reject combination with --isolated, detect is_git_repository via existsSync(join(path, '.git')). When the path is under no registered project_targets row of the chosen project, print an informational note suggesting pan project add-target but do not fail (D-3). Update sync-sources/skills/pan-workspace/SKILL.md in the same commit (lint-skills rule). New test file per PRD WI-1.

items.title: Given an existing directory, pan workspace new x --target-path <dir> creates a scratch workspace row whose path column stores the resolved directory and whose is_git_repository reflects .git presence
The command rejects a nonexistent or non-directory --target-path and rejects --target-path combined with --isolated, exiting non-zero with an error naming the problem
When the target path is under no registered project target, the command prints an informational note suggesting pan project add-target and still creates the row
npx vitest run tests/unit/cli/workspace-new-target-path.test.ts exits 0 covering the happy path and both rejection cases

expected_outputs: workspace-new-target-path.test.ts completes with exit code 0 including the dry-run cases

narrative.Action: Per PRD WI-1 (FR-2, D-4): add a --dry-run flag to pan workspace new that prints the resolved intent as JSON ({projectId, kind, name, path, branchName, parentBranch, parentBranchGuessed, isGitRepository, wouldCreateWorktree}) and returns BEFORE the isolated git worktree add and before createWorkspace, so no DB row, no worktree, and no memory home is created. Extend the WI-1 test file with dry-run assertions that verify via the resolver (listWorkspaces) that no row was written.

items.title: pan workspace new x --dry-run prints intent JSON containing projectId, kind, name, path, branchName, parentBranch, parentBranchGuessed, isGitRepository, and wouldCreateWorktree
After a --dry-run invocation (shared and --isolated variants), the resolver returns no new workspace row and no worktree directory exists on disk
--dry-run combined with --target-path prints the resolved target directory as path and wouldCreateWorktree false
relocateWorkspace writer + pan workspace relocate

narrative.Action: Per PRD WI-2 (FR-3, D-2, D-5): add relocateWorkspace(id, path) to src/lib/workspaces/writer.ts next to archiveWorkspace — validate the row exists and is not archived, refuse kind='issue', require --force for kind='main' (warn about projects.yaml divergence), then UPDATE path, is_git_repository, last_accessed_at and re-write the memory-home metadata.json through the existing identity-record writer (atomic tmp+rename). Add workspaceRelocateCommand resolving <ws> via resolveWorkspaceRef and printing old → new path; register pan workspace relocate <ws> --path <dir> [--force]. Ensure pan workspace get <ws> prints the memory-home path (D-2), adding it if absent. Update sync-sources/skills/pan-workspace/SKILL.md in the same commit. All child processes via async execFile only (NFR-2).

items.title: pan workspace relocate on a scratch workspace updates the path column, refreshes is_git_repository, rewrites memory-home metadata.json, and touches last_accessed_at
relocate refuses kind='issue' workspaces and archived workspaces with a non-zero exit and guidance; main without --force is refused while main with --force succeeds with a divergence warning
pan workspace get <ws> prints the workspace's memory-home path
scripts/guard-workspace-doors.sh exits 0 with the new writer function (all registry writes stay behind the write door)
pan memory search --target: target-scoped recall

metadata.readinessReason: First item in the memory-CLI chain; no other ready item shares src/lib/memory/cli.ts or src/cli/commands/memory.ts, and the new resolver read is additive.

narrative.Action: Per PRD WI-3 (FR-4): add listWorkspacesForPath(path) to src/lib/workspaces/resolver.ts near resolveWorkspaceForCwd — realpath both sides, all projects, is_archived=0 by default. Extend searchMemory in src/lib/memory/cli.ts with targetPath support that fans out per matched workspace's project FTS filtered by those workspace ids and merges by rank, reusing the --global merging code path. Add --target [path] to the search command in src/cli/commands/memory.ts: bare --target defaults to cwd; mutually exclusive with --workspace/--issue/--global; zero matches prints a friendly 'no workspaces target <dir>' note and exits 0. Update sync-sources/skills/pan-memory/SKILL.md in the same commit.

items.title: Given two workspaces in different projects sharing one target directory, pan memory search q --target <dir> returns merged rank-ordered hits from both workspaces
listWorkspacesForPath resolves symlinked directories via realpath and excludes archived workspaces by default
--target combined with --workspace, --issue, or --global exits non-zero naming the exclusivity rule; bare --target defaults to the current working directory
When no workspace targets the directory, the command prints a 'no workspaces target <dir>' note and exits 0
Workspace-addressed pan memory status/summary + --history

narrative.Action: Per PRD WI-4 (FR-5/6/7, D-8): make the status and summary issue positionals optional and add --workspace <ref> plus --history <n> (status only). Resolution order: --workspace via resolveWorkspaceRef; issue positional via the existing getWorkspaceForIssue path; neither → resolveWorkspaceForCwd(process.cwd()); nothing resolvable → actionable error naming all three addressing modes. Add getMemoryStatusForWorkspace and getMemoryStatusHistory (delegating to readArchivedStatuses, default 3 untouched for synthesis, CLI cap 50) to src/lib/memory/cli.ts. History output prints current status first then archived newest-first with updatedAt/headline/phase; --json emits {current, history}. Update sync-sources/skills/pan-memory/SKILL.md in the same commit.

items.title: pan memory status --workspace <ref> resolves by id and by name and prints the same status.json content the issue-positional path prints for an issue workspace
--history N prints the current status followed by up to N archived statuses newest-first, N capped at 50; --json emits {current, history}
With neither positional nor --workspace, the command falls back to the cwd's workspace, and when nothing resolves it exits non-zero naming all three addressing modes
Each pan memory status <issue> and pan memory summary <issue> positional invocation produces output identical to before the change (regression assertions in the named test)

Implement by extending readRecentObservations in src/lib/memory/rollup.ts or adding a date-windowed sibling readObservationsSince(projectId, workspaceId, days). items.title: pan memory timeline prints chronological observation rows showing timestamp, actionStatus or summary, and files for the resolved workspace
--days windows the observations to the given day span, --limit caps the row count, and --json emits structured rows

pan memory read with realpath containment

expected_outputs: timeline-read.test.ts completes with exit code 0 including every traversal-rejection case

narrative.Action: Per PRD WI-5 (FR-9, D-9, NFR-4): add pan memory read <path> [--from N] [--lines M] printing a file from the resolved workspace's memory home. Containment: realpath(join(memoryRoot, userPath)) must start with realpath(memoryRoot) + sep, mirroring the symlink-safe check in src/lib/memory/pin-path.ts; reject absolute input paths outright. Claude Code JSONL session files under ~/.claude must be unreachable by construction. Ship the traversal test matrix (../ traversal, absolute path, symlink escaping the home) in the same commit. Update sync-sources/skills/pan-memory/SKILL.md in the same commit.

items.title: pan memory read <relative path> prints the file's content and --from/--lines return the requested line slice
The command rejects ../ traversal, absolute input paths, and symlinks whose realpath escapes the memory home, each with a non-zero exit
The containment check rejects a path constructed to point at a ~/.claude JSONL session file, proven by a named test assertion

SessionStart standing briefing with per-session dedup

metadata.readinessReason: Touches only the hooks route and a brand-new module; no other plan item shares src/dashboard/server/routes/hooks.ts or src/lib/memory/session-briefing.ts.
expected_outputs: build completes so the boot path can be runtime-tested on a throwaway instance

narrative.Action: Per PRD WI-6 (FR-10, D-7, NFR-6): create src/lib/memory/session-briefing.ts composing a briefing from readCurrentStatus + readRecentObservations + pinned-doc titles via the existing pin reader — local files only, no LLM call, bounded by a new SESSION_START_MEMORY_BUDGETS constant beside PROMPT_TIME_MEMORY_BUDGETS. In handleMemorySessionStartBody (src/dashboard/server/routes/hooks.ts), on 'accepted' additionally compose the briefing and include it in the HTTP response for the hook script to emit as SessionStart additionalContext. Write the dedup marker rag-runs/injected-<sessionId>.json ({sessionId, writtenAt, byteSize}) first; if it exists, return the briefing-less response. Any composition error logs and degrades to current behavior. IMPLEMENTATION CHECKPOINT (PRD WI-6): verify how the installed SessionStart hook script consumes the route response and how Claude Code expects hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext before wiring; fallback is first-prompt-per-session delivery via the existing UserPromptSubmit path with the same dedup marker. Boot-path discipline: runtime-boot-test on a throwaway instance before the live server runs this; any delay-based test uses vi.useFakeTimers (NFR-3).

items.title: A fresh session's SessionStart (or the documented first-prompt fallback) receives a rendered briefing containing status headline/goal/phase/nextSteps, a recent-observations digest, and pinned-doc titles, within SESSION_START_MEMORY_BUDGETS
When the dedup marker rag-runs/injected-<sessionId>.json exists, the route returns the briefing-less response, so a session id receives at most one briefing
A composition failure logs and returns the current briefing-less accepted response, and disabled observations still return 'disabled' unchanged
Composition performs no LLM call and reads only local files, and the change survives a runtime boot of the built dashboard server on a throwaway instance
memoryPhase in the workspace-registry list DTO

narrative.Action: Per PRD WI-8 (D-12): the GET /api/workspace-registry list handler attaches memoryPhase: string | null per row, read server-side via readCurrentStatus(projectId, workspaceId).phase ?? null, and only for kind !== 'issue' (issue rows return null without status reads). No per-row client fetches; status reads are small local JSON files. Existing DTO fields stay untouched (no-loss). The planning addendum confirmed no workspace-registry DTO lives in packages/contracts — the shape is owned by the route.

items.title: The list response contains memoryPhase with the status.json phase for main/scratch rows that have a status file and null for rows without one

The Cmd-K workspaces scope in CommandPalette.tsx applies the same default filter. GET /api/workspace-registry keeps returning all kinds — this filter is presentation-side only. Badge/row styling follows the pan-style-guide (no decorative color). Frontend tests are colocated per the planning addendum. Playwright screenshots at narrow and wide widths are verified by the implementer, never the operator.

rebuild-workspaces archives terminal-issue rows

Archival goes through archiveWorkspace on the write door (NFR-1).
